facts.statement: The genus Machimosaurus was named by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1837.
facts.quote: authority: Von Meyer, 1837

facts.statement: Machimosaurus is the largest known crocodyliform from the Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Machimosaurus is the largest known crocodyliform of the Jurassic.

facts.statement: Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer originally named isolated conical, blunt teeth from Switzerland as Madrimosaurus hugii in 1837.
facts.quote: Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1837 named isolated conical, blunt teeth with numerous longitudinal lines from Switzerland, Madrimosaurus hugii.

facts.statement: In 1838, von Meyer corrected the misspelling to Machimosaurus, derived from Greek words meaning "pugnacious lizard".
facts.quote: However, in 1838, realising he had misspelled the name, he emended Madrimosaurus to Machimosaurus, from the Greek machimoi, ancient Egyptian troops deployed during the Ptolemaic Dynasty plus the -saurus suffix, literally meaning "pugnacious lizard".

facts.statement: Machimosaurus teeth are characterized by a rounded, blunt apex and stout morphology, making them easily distinguishable from other teleosaurid teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth of Machimosaurus, with their rounded, blunt apex and stout morphology make them characteristic and easily identifiable compared to other teleosaurid teeth.

facts.statement: Machimosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian and Tithonian) and Early Cretaceous periods.
facts.quote: Machimosaurus is an extinct genus of machimosaurid crocodyliform from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian and Tithonian) and Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Fossils of Machimosaurus have been found in Switzerland, England, France, Germany, Portugal, and Tunisia.
facts.quote: The type species, Machimosaurus hugii, was found in Switzerland. Other fossils have been found in England, France, Germany, Portugal, Switzerland and Tunisia.

facts.statement: Bite marks on a sauropod femur from Switzerland match teeth of Machimosaurus hugii, suggesting it fed on sauropods.
facts.quote: Bite marks on an early Kimmeridgian sauropod (Amanzia) femur from Switzerland match teeth known from Machimosaurus hugii, also found in the same deposits.

facts.statement: Morphofunctional analysis of the skull suggests Machimosaurus specialized in eating turtles.
facts.quote: Morphofunctional analysis on the skull of Machimosaurus strongly suggests they ate turtles (chelonophagy).

facts.statement: The teeth of Machimosaurus are morphologically adapted for seizing and crushing hard prey.
facts.quote: Morphological comparison of their teeth also confirms that they are adapted to seizing and crushing hard prey.

facts.statement: Vertebrae articulations indicate Machimosaurus lived in open seas, swimming via lateral tail undulations while using limbs for steering and balance.
facts.quote: Based on the vertebrae (zygapophysial) articulations, Machimosaurus is considered to have lived in open-seas, swimming by lateral undulations of the tail with the limbs used for steering and balancing.

facts.statement: Large basioccipital tubera suggest well-developed head and neck muscles, assisting Machimosaurus in diving.
facts.quote: Head and neck depressing (downward moving) muscles would have been well-developed, as their attachment site on the skull (basioccipital tubera) were large. This would have greatly assisted Machimosaurus in diving.

facts.statement: The genus includes species such as M. hugii, M. mosae, M. nowackianus, M. buffetauti, and M. rex.
facts.quote: subdivision: M. hugii type Von Meyer (1837) M. mosae Sauvage and Lienard 1879 M. nowackianus (von Huene. 1938) M. buffetauti Young et al., 2015 M. rex Fanti et al., 2016

facts.statement: Machimosaurus belongs to the family Teleosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Teleosauridae

facts.statement: Machimosaurus is classified within the suborder Thalattosuchia.
facts.quote: subordo: Thalattosuchia

facts.statement: Machimosaurus lived between the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian and Tithonian) and Early Cretaceous (Berriasian and Hauterivian) periods.
facts.quote: Machimosaurus es un género extinto de crocodiliforme teleosáurido, que vivió entre los períodos Jurásico Superior (Kimmeridgiense y Titoniense) y el Cretácico Inferior (Berriasiense y Hauteriviense).

facts.statement: Machimosaurus went extinct during the Hauterivian, making it the last of the teleosaurids.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Machimosaurus se extinguió durante el Hauteriviense, siendo así el último de los teleosáuridos.

facts.statement: Machimosaurus rex, described in 2016 from Tunisia, is the largest known teleosaurid, estimated at 9.6 meters long and weighing nearly three tons.
facts.quote: En 2016, una nueva especie de Machimosaurus descubierta en Túnez fue descrita en la revista Cretaceous Research. Nombrada Machimosaurus rex, es el teleosáurido de mayor tamaño que se conozca, con una longitud total estimada en 9.6 metros y con un peso de cerca de tres toneladas, con base en un esqueleto parcial.

facts.statement: Machimosaurus rex represents the most recent record of a teleosaurid, originating from the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: M. rex además constituye el registro más reciente de un teleosáurido, ya que procede del Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: It is uncertain whether ichnofossils of a gigantic crocodylomorph from Spain belong to Machimosaurus.
facts.quote: Ichnofossils of a gigantic Crocodylomorph from Spain may belong to Machimosaurus,but the taxonomic attribution is uncertain.

facts.statement: Machimosaurus lived between 165.3 and 113.2 million years ago during the Callovian to Aptian periods.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Aptian (165.3 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Machimosaurus belongs to the subfamily Machimosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Machimosaurini

facts.statement: Machimosaurus is classified within the family Machimosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Machimosauridae

facts.statement: Fossils of Machimosaurus have been found in the semi-aquatic deposits of Oker, Lower Saxony, Germany, dating to the Kimmeridgian age.
facts.quote: De los depósitos semiacuáticos de Oker, Baja Sajonia, Alemania, de edad Kimmeridgiense se conocen dos géneros de teleosáuridos, Steneosaurus y Machimosaurus

facts.statement: Machimosaurus is also found alongside Steneosaurus in Titonian age deposits in western France.
facts.quote: Machimosaurus y Steneosaurus son también hallados juntos en los mismos yacimientos de edad Titoniana del oeste de Francia

facts.statement: Bite marks on a Cetiosauriscus femur from the early Kimmeridgian of Switzerland match the known teeth of Machimosaurus hugii.
facts.quote: Marcas de mordidas en un fémur del saurópodo Cetiosauriscus de principios del Kimmeridgiense de Suiza encajan con los dientes conocidos de Machimosaurus hugii

facts.statement: Fossil turtles from the Kimmeridgian Solothurn Limestone in northern Switzerland show bite marks and contain chipped Machimosaurus teeth embedded in their shells.
facts.quote: Tortugas fósiles del Kimmeridgiense de la formación de calizas "Solothurn Turtle" del norte de Suiza tienen marcas de mordidas, y tienen dientes astillados de Machimosaurus alojados en sus caparazones

facts.statement: Morphofunctional analysis of the skull suggests Machimosaurus regularly ate turtles.
facts.quote: Análisis morfofuncionales del cráneo de Machimosaurus sugieren con rotundidad que esta especie comía regularmente tortugas

facts.statement: Morphological comparisons of its teeth confirm Machimosaurus was adapted to capture and crush hard prey.
facts.quote: Comparaciones morfológicas de sus dientes también confirman que se encontraban adaptados para capturar y destrozar presas duras

facts.statement: Based on vertebrae zygapophysis joints, Machimosaurus likely lived in open seas, swimming with lateral tail undulations while its legs steered and balanced the body.
facts.quote: Basándose en las articulaciones de las zigapófisis de las vértebras, se considera que Machimosaurus vivía en mares abiertos, nadando con ondulaciones laterales de su cola mientras que sus patas timoneaban y balanceaban el cuerpo

facts.statement: Machimosaurus likely had well-developed muscle depressions on its head and neck for downward movements and a large basioccipital tuberosity attachment site.
facts.quote: Las depresiones musculares de la cabeza y el cuello (para los movimientos descendentes) debieron haber estado bien desarrolladas, y su sitio de acoplamiento en el cráneo (tuberosidad basioccipital) era grande

facts.statement: These anatomical features were likely very useful for Machimosaurus to submerge itself.
facts.quote: En conjunto estas características debieron haberle sido de gran utilidad al Machimosaurus para sumergirse

rejected.statement: Machimosaurus rex is the largest named teleosauroid and thalattosuchian, reaching an estimated length of up to 7.15 meters with a skull length of 155 cm.
rejected.quote: Machimosaurus rex is the largest named teleosauroid and thalattosuchian, with an estimated length of up to 7.15 m (skull length 155 cm).
